shape_hint: Machine screw with a pan head (flat bearing face, slightly domed top with rounded edge) and a cross recess (type H Phillips or type Z Pozidriv); head diameter dk about twice the thread diameter, head height k about 0.75 d.
notes: Only pitch, dk and k reach three clusters, for M2, M2.5, M3, M4, M5, M6, M8, M10. The ISO 7045 specific head sizes rest on: M2.5 k 2.1 - globalfastener, engineersedge, keller-kalmbach, nfgab, schrauben-lexikon; M3 dk 5.6 - globalfastener, engineersedge, nfgab (exactly three); M5 dk 9.5 and k 3.7 - globalfastener, engineersedge, keller-kalmbach, nfgab. fasten.it prints the older DIN 7985 numbers in these places (k 2 / dk 6 / dk 10, k 3.8) and schrauben-lexikon prints k 3.8 for M5. nfgab's 'k max ISO/DIN' row gives the DIN 7985 maxima (1.72, 2.52, 3.25, 4.75, 6.15) for the sizes where it prints one number, so it dissents on k for M2, M3, M4, M6, M8 - the kept k values still have 4-5 clusters. M3.5 is dropped: k 2.6 on globalfastener only (fasten.it 2.7), dk 7 and pitch 0.6 on two clusters. All tolerance columns (a max, b min, da max, dk min, k min, r min) exist only in the globalfastener table (fullerfasteners repeats it with the same wording), so none can be kept. fasteners.eu's ISO 7045 page states 'Table according to DIN 7985' and is not counted; westfieldfasteners' page is a DIN 7985 page and was not used; schrauben-lexikon's 'd2' row is unexplained on the page and was not used. Pitch on engineersedge is read from the thread designation (e.g. 'M3X0.5'). dk and k on engineersedge, keller-kalmbach and nfgab (dk) are nominal values without the word 'max'; the column is 'nominal = max' as stated by globalfastener and fasten.it. Würth e-shop pages (JavaScript, access denied to automated fetch) could not be read.

verification.checks_done: Verifier re-fetched every page itself on 2026-11-11 with curl (browser UA, 2.5 s pause per host; HTTP 200 for all; globalfastener detail_400 needed one retry after a 403), wrote its own stdlib HTML table reader (vt.py, gf.py, obs.py) and counting script (count.py) without using the researcher's raw/, extracted tables or scripts. Drawings that define bare symbols (schrauben-lexikon gifs, nfgab pngs) were fetched and viewed. Lead decisions applied: amesweb (calculator) not a source; a rival value printed by 2+ independent lineages removes the row; cells of another standard printed under the target title (verified equal to that standard's table) are neither support nor rival; pages reproducing the standard's text (boltport ISO 4035) excluded. A cluster whose own pages give two different values for a cell is not counted for it. Largest rectangle (cells, then rows) chosen among column subsets that contain the drawing keys. Re-counted 8 x 3 candidate cells; kept 8 x 3; per-cell clusters in ms-pan.verify.md.
problems: Pitch rests on exactly three clusters (GF, FI, EE); EE pitch is read from its 'M3X0.5' designations.
M3 dk 5.6 has exactly three clusters (GF, EE, NFG 'd2 ISO/DIN 5,6/6'); NFG d2 counted only because its drawing (1319r.png, verified) labels d2 as head diameter.

Rule-3 interpretation: fasten.it (M2.5 k 2, M3 dk 6, M5 dk 10 / k 3.8), schrauben-lexikon+boltport (M5 k 3.8) and nfgab single 'k max' values (1.72, 2.52, 3.25, 4.75, 6.15) equal DIN 7985 numbers and were treated as another standard's cells, not rivals. Under a literal reading of the 2-page rival rule M2.5, M3 and M5 would go.
EE, KK and NFG give head diameter/height without max/min; counted as the nominal (= max) value. GF and FI state nom=max explicitly.
